newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch, Paine Webber post record profits.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch, Paine Webber post record profits.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. reported a 14 percent rise in first-quarter profits Tuesday, crediting robust market activity for the highest quarterly earnings in the brokerage and investment bank's 112-year history.
Brokerage PaineWebber Group Inc. also reported record profits and revenues in a quarter that saw the stock market rally to record levels in early March before starting a major sell-off.

Merill Lynch reported profits of $465 million, or $2.34 a share, easily beating the consensus Wall Street analyst forecast of $2.07 a share, according to the First Call service, which tracks analyst predictions.
The earnings represented a 14 percent increase from first-quarter 1996 profits of $410 million, or $2.03 a share.

The New York-based company, founded in 1885, also said its board approved a one-third increase in its quarterly dividend, from 30 cents a share to 40 cents, and a two-for-one stock split, payable May 30 in the form of a stock dividend.
Merrill Lynch's stock jumped $2.375 to $90.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Net revenues hit a record $3.8 billion, up 18 percent from the year-ago first quarter's $3.3 billion, with increases in all revenue categories, the company said.

"I couldn't be more optimistic about our company's prospects," Merrill Lynch Chief Executive Officer David Komansky told reporters after the company's annual meeting in Plainsboro, N.J. He also said a correction in the stock market was healthy and re-established a bedrock for stock prices.
Since hitting a record of 7,085.16 on March 11, the Dow Jones industrial average has headed sharply lower. On Tuesday the blue-chip index rose 135 points to end at 6,587.

PaineWebber reported a smaller increase in net quarterly profits, to $100.8 million, or 99 cents a share, from $100.5 million, or 96 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996, but said the earnings were the biggest in the company's 117-year history.
The earnings handily beat analysts' consesus forecast of 87 cents a share, according to First Call. Paine Webber's stock edged up 87.5 cents to $32 on the NYSE.
PaineWebber had net revenues of $984 million, compared with $962 million in last year's first quarter.
The brokerages' rosy earnings reports came a day after investment banking firm Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. reported higher-than-expected first-quarter earnings.
Merrill Lynch said total assets in its worldwide client accounts reached a record $868 billion at the end of the first quarter, up $137 billion from the year-ago quarter.
Merrill Lynch said it racked up quarterly records in revenues from commissions, principal transactions, investment banking and asset management and portfolio service fees.

"Our record quarterly earnings were the result of the strength and diversity of our franchise geographically and by market segment, as well as robust market activity that prevailed through much of the quarter, before slowing in March," Merrill Lynch Chairman Daniel Tully and Komansky said in a joint statement.

Commission revenues totalled $1.1 billion, up 13 percent from first-quarter 1996, while principal transaction revenues -- derived from trades on Merrill's own accounts -- were also $1.1 billion, an 8 percent rise.
Investment banking revenues soared 61 percent to $608 million. Asset management and portfolio service fees increased 20 percent to $646 million.

Merrill said its U.S. and global first-quarter market shares of underwriting of debt and stocks were 16.1 percent and 13.2 percent, respectively, according to Securities Data Co. Securities Data said Merrill had a 19.8 percent market share of worldwide stock and stock-linked offerings in the first quarter.
